checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated head with prominent jaw bearing large fang-like teeth.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fish has an elongated head, but the mouth structure resembles a duck-bill (typical of Pike/Esox lucius) rather than the protruding lower jaw with fangs of a Barracouta. Teeth are not clearly visible as large fangs.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wide mouth with protruding lower jaw.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The upper jaw appears to extend further or equal to the lower jaw (duck-bill shape), contradicting the 'protruding lower jaw' characteristic of the Barracouta/Snoek.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated streamlined body with notably extended proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body is significantly elongated and cylindrical/streamlined.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Small silvery scales with bluish-green dorsal coloration.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fish displays a distinct pattern of light spots on a darker greenish/brown background (chain-link or reticulated pattern), which is characteristic of Northern Pike, not the uniform silvery/bluish-green of a Barracouta.
A lateral line is faintly visible running along the flank.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Separated dorsal fins; first dorsal spiny, second dorsal soft-rayed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only one dorsal fin is clearly visible, positioned far back near the tail (posterior). Barracoutas have two separated dorsal fins located more centrally/anteriorly. This anatomy matches Esox (Pike).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anal fin similar to second dorsal.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: An anal fin is present and positioned opposite the single dorsal fin, consistent with the visible anatomy (though inconsistent with the target class).

The fingers gripping the fish appear slightly fused and lack clear nail definition, blending into the fish's body texture slightly.
Slight warping in the grass line behind the man, typical of generative backgrounds.
